subject: Aurora PoC — model-fit, throughput tuning & AWQ/GPTQ tradeoffs

Subject: Aurora PoC — initial call recap & next steps

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great to learn more about Aurora's ingestion pipeline and the latency targets for your realtime summarization feature. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Goals we heard: 99th pct latency < 220ms for single-turn summarization at median length 160 tokens; throughput target ~120 reqs/s per replica.
- Primary constraints: customer PII removal on ingest, on-prem deployment in AWS us-west-2, and cost target ~ $0.002 / request (token-normalized).
- Suggested model candidates to validate: Mistral-Instant-8B, Llama-3-13B (FP8 baseline), and Falcon-40B-instruct (for worst-case quality checks).

Immediate next steps (we propose):
1) Redwood will provision a small PoC workspace (hosted trial or dedicated dev pool) and run a short eval across three model/quant stacks: AWQ 4-bit, GPTQ 4-bit, and FP8 (for L3/13B).
2) We'll run your prompt set (please see attached aurora_prompt-set-v1.txt) and return top-line metrics: latency p50/p95/p99, token cost, and a small quality sweep (ROUGE/precision heuristics + human spot checks).
3) Meet Wed 2026-11-12 to review preliminary numbers and pick a tuning path.

I'll attach the prompt set and a lightweight benchmark plan; Karthik & Monica are looped for ops and procurement questions. Let me know if Wed works and whether Tom should join.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Rishi — thanks for the clear summary. Wed works for a quick sync (Tom and I can do 10:00 PT). A couple of clarifications before you run the eval:

- Can you include a column in the benchmark for hallucination-sensitive prompts? We have ~15 prompts that are high-risk for incorrect facts.
- For the cost budgeting, we prefer to see cost per 1k tokens and per-request for 160-token medians.
- How disruptive is switching between AWQ and FP8 during a rollout? We expect to want the cheapest config in steady-state but may need a higher-quality fallback.

Also, curious if you can comment on expected quality deltas between AWQ 4-bit and GPTQ 4-bit for Mistral-Instant-8B — we saw mixed results in earlier tests.

Thanks,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-12T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Aurora PoC — initial call recap & next steps

Sara — good questions. Short answers up top, longer notes below.

- Hallucination column: yes — we'll add a binary hallucination flag from our evaluator plus a short human annotation on edge cases for the 15 high-risk prompts.
- Cost reporting: we'll provide both cost/1k tokens and cost/request for the 160-token baseline you gave.
- AWQ ↔ FP8 rollouts: switching is low-friction at the routing layer — Redwood supports per-route fallback policies (e.g., use AWQ primary, FP8 fallback) with model-variant pinning. The operational complexity is modest: you need a compatible runtime variant for each quantization format and a short warmup for KV caches.

More detail on model/quant tradeoffs (what we'll run in the PoC):

1) Mistral-Instant-8B (target: best cost/latency)
   - AWQ 4-bit: expected throughput +30–60% vs GPTQ 4-bit with small quality delta on standard prompts. Historically, AWQ preserves logits for many dense MLP layers better; we often see small drops on hallucination-sensitive prompts.
   - GPTQ 4-bit: slightly lower throughput, usually a touch higher robustness on factual prompts in our internal tests; more variability depending on calibration.
   - FP8 (mixed): baseline for quality; higher token cost but much lower regression risk. Good as a fallback.

2) Llama-3-13B (baseline FP8 and mixed-precision)
   - FP8 baseline gives best quality for long-context and instruction-following. AWQ/4-bit variants exist but we recommend conservative tuning (AWQ 6-bit or FP8 for Aurora's hallucination-sensitive items).

3) Falcon-40B (spot-check)
   - Only for worst-case quality checks (we won't run all quant variants by default due to cost).

Preliminary perf expectations (PoC scale, single GPU profile):
- Mistral-Instant-8B AWQ4: p50 ~ 55ms, p95 ~ 140ms, p99 ~ 260ms; throughput ~150 reqs/s.
- Mistral-Instant-8B GPTQ4: p50 ~ 70ms, p95 ~ 180ms, p99 ~ 320ms; throughput ~110–120 reqs/s.
- Llama-3-13B FP8: p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 260ms, p99 ~ 420ms; throughput ~40–60 reqs/s.

Quality note: our AWQ/4-bit tests show a 2–6% delta in our automatic hallucination metric compared to FP8 on high-risk prompts (varies by prompt). We will surface human-checked failure examples so you can evaluate acceptability.

Deliverables for next meeting (we'll upload into the Drive link below):
- bench_awq_vs_gptq.csv with latency/cost/auto-quality flags per prompt
- 20 human spot-checks for hallucination-sensitive prompts
- Recommended rollout plan (primary AWQ4 + FP8 fallback for routes flagged as high-risk)
- A short addendum: estimated monthly cost at target throughput and an ops checklist for KV cache warmup and routing policy.

I'll drop the Drive link and a short SOW draft in this thread by EOD today. See attached template for the benchmark.

Cheers,
Rishi
